source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Biologically Inspired Design Concept Generation Using GPT
finding: Fine-tuned GPT-3 (Davinci) on AskNature innovation entries to retrieve a biological analogue and map it to a design concept. Three generator types differ in what the problem input is (application; benefits plus application; challenge).
numbers: Fine-tuning data from AskNature. 50 concepts per generator per case. Flying-car case study.
limits: Single case study; AskNature entries are hand-curated success stories, so the model may only replay known analogies. No no-fine-tune baseline.
agent_relevance: Shows analogue retrieval can be done by a model, but only as a generation step with no check on where the analogue came from.

source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Biologically Inspired Design Concept Generation Using GPT
finding: Relevancy classifiers (GPT-3 Curie) were fine-tuned to check whether a generated concept fits the problem and the biology. Nature-solution link was easy to learn; problem-solution link was harder.
numbers: Validation accuracy after 4 epochs: benefits-innovation 75.3%, challenge-innovation 79.8%. Biomimicry-innovation 89.9% after 1 epoch, 94.4% after 2. Each set 442 samples (221 positive from AskNature, 221 generated negatives), 4:1 train/validation.
limits: Negatives were themselves model-generated, so the classifier may learn the generator's style. The 2022 preprint of the same work reported 67.4% and 97.8%, so the numbers moved between versions.
agent_relevance: A learned relevance gate can screen analogues, but it is weakest on the part that matters most: does the analogue solve THIS problem.

source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Biologically Inspired Design Concept Generation Using GPT
finding: Diversity of generated concepts depends on how tight the problem input is. Open input (application only) gave the most diverse concepts, near the diversity of the AskNature robotics set; challenge input gave the least.
numbers: Word Mover's Distance on Word2Vec; 3 AskNature robot samples x 50 concepts x 3 types = 450 concepts. Baseline: 36 AskNature robotics innovations.
limits: Word2Vec trained on Google News, not a design-aware metric. Three seed samples only.
agent_relevance: Looser problem framing widens analogue search; tight framing narrows it. Matches a stage-wise rule: widen first, then constrain.

source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Biologically Inspired Design Concept Generation Using GPT
finding: Retrieved source organisms clustered on near, attribute-matched animals. Birds came first, then insects, for a flying-car problem. A few plants and reptiles also appeared.
numbers: Birds in over 50% of retrieved analogues across all three generator types. Share of concepts passing the relevancy classifiers: 58% to 84% depending on type and check (table partly garbled in the text layer).
limits: The paper itself ties this to human attribute-similarity retrieval. No count of how many analogues were far-field.
agent_relevance: Same near-field bias humans show. An agent needs an explicit step that pushes retrieval away from the obvious source domain.

source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Biologically Inspired Design Concept Generation Using GPT
finding: Design team rated selected concepts on feasibility and novelty. Open generators scored higher novelty but lower feasibility; the challenge generator scored more feasible but less novel. A bird-bone porous-structure concept scored the highest novelty with acceptable feasibility.
numbers: 9 of 10 returned surveys usable. 5-point rubrics. Two concepts per type rated, after filtering by the classifiers.
limits: Tiny rater pool, one team, one project. Only concepts that passed the classifiers were rated.
agent_relevance: The novelty-feasibility trade-off follows problem framing, not just temperature. Useful as a lever the program can set.

source: Zhu, Zhang, Luo (2022) Generative Pre-Trained Transformers for Biologically Inspired Design
finding: Earlier preprint of the same GPT-3 bio-inspired design method. Same pipeline, different evaluator numbers and pass rates than the later version.
numbers: Preprint classifier accuracy: benefits-innovation 67.4%, challenge-innovation 79.8%, biomimicry-innovation 97.8% after 1 epoch. Pass rates listed include 86%, 90%, 44%, 40%, 76%, 84%.
limits: Version drift. Cite the later version for final numbers and note the change.
agent_relevance: Reminder that tiny classifier sets give unstable accuracy; do not trust a single learned gate.

source: Emuna et al. (2023) Imitation of Life: A Search Engine for Biologically Inspired Design (BARCODE)
finding: BARCODE mines Wikipedia sentences for challenge and strategy pairs, so a plain-language engineering problem retrieves biological strategies. Uses NLI and data programming, not a generative LLM.
numbers: Strategy precision at top 7: 72% vs 36% for the baseline; top 15: 69% vs 29%. Challenge sentences lower (about 22% to 57%). Mann-Whitney p = 2.26e-7 (k=7), 2e-10 (k=15), strategy. 29 MTurk workers, 3 per sentence; Fleiss kappa 0.42 (challenge), 0.55 (strategy).
limits: Crowd labels only moderately consistent. Filtering to 3% of data hurt more at k=15. Baseline is a simple one.
agent_relevance: A retrieval target of challenge-plus-strategy pairs, not topical similarity, is the part worth copying.

source: Emuna et al. (2023) BARCODE
finding: Against a rule-based biomimetic retrieval method (Cheong and Shu 2014), BARCODE ranked inspirational sentences higher. Robust to paraphrased queries, with a larger gap on paraphrases.
numbers: Top 10 strict precision 0.56 vs 0.22; liberal 0.80 vs 0.25. 160 sentences, 4 verbs, scored 0-2 by 4 blind raters, mean pairwise Spearman 0.60.
limits: Only 4 verbs; raters were the authors' team.
agent_relevance: Query form matters. The agent should restate the problem as an abstract verb-object function before retrieval.

source: Emuna et al. (2023) BARCODE
finding: Three bio-engineering experts used the engine live. Many results matched ideas they already had; some were new.
numbers: 21% of relevant results were already known to the experts; 33% of relevant results rated highly interesting; all but three queries gave at least one very interesting result.
limits: Three experts, no control condition, no measure of whether ideas improved outcomes.
agent_relevance: Retrieval value is in the minority of surprising hits; expect most hits to be known or weak.

source: Emuna et al. (2023) BARCODE (background claims)
finding: Reports why analogue retrieval is a bottleneck: hand-curated biology databases (AskNature, DANE with Structure-Behavior-Function) are small and slow to build, and most biology papers carry no design insight.
numbers: DANE-style SBF description of one organism takes 40 to 100 hours. An audit found only 3.36% of 3,416 PubMed articles gave design insight (Kaiser et al. 2012).
limits: Both figures are quoted from earlier work as reported in this paper.
agent_relevance: Argues for automatic encoding of sources. An LLM can cut that cost but needs a check on what it writes.

source: Majumder, Bhattacharya, Chakrabarti (2024/2025) RAG tool for SAPPhIRE models
finding: GPT-4o writes a hypothetical SAPPhIRE description of a system, which is used to query Wikipedia chunks; GPT-3.5 then writes the final model. Aim: scale the encoding step of design-by-analogy.
numbers: Three test systems (orifice plate, thermo-electric cooler, solenoid valve). Mean groundedness 0.81 (n=183, CI 0.77-0.85), answer relevance 0.86 (n=210, CI 0.83-0.89), context relevance 0.79 (n=167, CI 0.76-0.83).
limits: Scores come from an LLM judge (TruLens, GPT-3.5), not from experts. Many judge calls failed, so samples dropped. Only three artificial systems; no check of analogy quality.
agent_relevance: Encoding by causal ontology is possible with an LLM, but quality was graded by another LLM, which our guardrails treat as weak evidence.

source: Majumder, Bhattacharya, Chakrabarti (2024/2025) RAG tool for SAPPhIRE models
finding: Groundedness was lower for some SAPPhIRE constructs (parts and organs), even though the judge still found the answers relevant.
numbers: Scores on 0-1; 0.8-1 high, 0.5-0.8 medium, below 0.5 low.
limits: Construct-level numbers only in a figure.
agent_relevance: Model fills in plausible parts that the retrieved text does not support. Keep source text attached to every claim.

source: Puranam, Sen, Workiewicz (2025) Can LLMs help improve analogical reasoning for strategic decisions
finding: Replicated Gick and Holyoak style transfer with a matching twist: two source stories, two target problems. Humans rarely used the right story spontaneously. GPT-4 without a hint almost never claimed the right story for the factory problem.
numbers: Humans n=199; GPT-4 n=60 runs (15 per condition). Human solve rate without hint: factory 6.3%, HR 20.3%; with hint: factory 8.7% (4 of 46), HR 37% (17 of 46). Original Gick and Holyoak 1983 Exp 2: 29% (8 of 28) without hint, 50% (14 of 28) with.
limits: Two problems; students; GPT-4 prompt wording matters; LLM runs were independent but one model.
agent_relevance: Humans need a cue to retrieve; the program, not the model, should supply the cue to try analogies.

source: Puranam, Sen, Workiewicz (2025) Can LLMs help improve analogical reasoning for strategic decisions
finding: A hint to use an analogy flipped GPT-4 from no use to full use. With the hint it found the right source every time but also claimed wrong sources about half the time. Humans were the reverse: few claims, but accurate.
numbers: GPT-4 no hint: Radiation analogy used 1 of 15; Dolphin 14 of 15; correct-story precision 0.00 and recall 0.00 (Radiation and Dolphin). With hint: recall 1.00, precision about 0.52, F1 0.67-0.68, accuracy 50-53%. Humans with hint: precision 0.67-0.75, recall 0.26-0.39, F1 0.38-0.51, accuracy 57-63%. Human no-hint Dolphin: precision 1.00, recall 0.22.
limits: The abstract describes GPT-4 as high recall; in the no-hint table recall is zero, so the headline holds only when cued. Small n; tables partly garbled in text extraction.
agent_relevance: High recall, low precision means a model proposes many analogues and needs a separate mapping check on each. Do not accept an analogue because the model likes it.

source: Puranam, Sen, Workiewicz (2025) Can LLMs help improve analogical reasoning for strategic decisions
finding: Authors argue the weak step is matching (causal mapping), not retrieval. Model failures came from surface similarity; human failures came from subtler causal misreadings.
numbers: Qualitative error analysis of the same samples.
limits: Authors' interpretation; not a separate test.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-checked mapping step: list the causal relations of the source and test each against the target before use.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR)
finding: Analogical prompting asks the model to recall relevant solved problems and then solve the target. No labelled examples or retrieval index. Beats 0-shot CoT and fixed 5-shot CoT across several base models.
numbers: GSM8K: GPT-3.5-turbo 5-shot CoT 75.0%, self-generated exemplars 75.8%-77.8% across variants. MATH (GPT-3.5): 33.0% vs 33.9-37.3%. text-davinci-003 GSM8K: 14.8% (text) vs 50.3-61.0%. Average gain about +4% across tasks.
limits: Variant rows in the extracted table lost their labels. Gains on GSM8K for GPT-3.5 are small (under 3 points).
agent_relevance: Cheap form of analogue retrieval from the model's own memory. Good for exemplar recall, unlike far-field cross-domain transfer.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR)
finding: Self-generated exemplars help only with strong models; with weak models, retrieved exemplars from a labelled set are better. Number of exemplars matters: one exemplar hurts.
numbers: GSM8K by scale: text-curie-001 2%, text-davinci-001 9%, text-davinci-002 about 48%, text-davinci-003 up to 61% for the method vs 54-57% for retrieved 5-shot CoT. K=1 underperforms, K=3 or 5 best (MATH K=4 gives 37.3).
limits: Authors state that self-generation fails when the model lacks relevant knowledge.
agent_relevance: Self-recall of analogues is a capability that shrinks with weaker models; a small model in our loop would need an external case store.

source: Yasunaga et al. (2024) Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners (ICLR)
finding: Adding self-generated knowledge (core concepts) before exemplars helped on competitive code generation; GPT-3.5 with the method came near GPT-4 plain.
numbers: Codeforces Acc@1: GPT-3.5 with method 15% vs GPT-4 with 3-shot CoT 16%. Plain 3-shot CoT 8% (one model row).
limits: Row labels in table lost in extraction; numbers read from text.
agent_relevance: Analogue prompting is one input to a loop, not a replacement for a solver check.

source: Ma, Grandi, McComb, Goucher-Lambert (2023) Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
finding: GPT-3 (davinci-003) generated 100 solutions for each of 12 design problems and was compared with crowdsourced solutions. Experts rated LLM solutions more feasible and useful, crowd solutions more novel. Few-shot prompting pulled output closer to crowd solutions but cut diversity.
numbers: 12 problems; temperature 0.9; adding unique adjective in the prompt gave lowest mean cosine similarity 0.746 (SD 0.06). Expert ratings on 0-2 anchored scales for feasibility, novelty, usefulness.
limits: Not analogy specific. Embedding novelty measure is a proxy.
agent_relevance: LLM default is feasible but common ideas. Analogue stimuli are a way to buy novelty back.

source: Kargupta, Mehri, Hakkani-Tur, Han (2026) Idea-Catalyst
finding: A pipeline restates a research goal as a domain-agnostic problem, retrieves papers from other disciplines, ranks source domains by interdisciplinary potential, then ideates. Control steps came from metacognition (assess goal, know the domain's open problems, pick sources on purpose).
numbers: Qwen3-14B generator (temp 0.7); gpt-oss-120b judge. Average relative gains over Guided Dual-Retrieval: novelty +21.38% (idea level), insightfulness +16.22% (takeaway level); insightfulness +282.21% vs Free-Form Source Retrieval.
limits: Win rates are by an LLM judge; relevance and usefulness competitive, not better. Outputs judged verbose.
agent_relevance: Closest published match to O7 as a loop: abstract the problem first, retrieve far on purpose. Gains are modest and judged by a model.

source: Kargupta, Mehri, Hakkani-Tur, Han (2026) Idea-Catalyst
finding: Free-form LLM source selection stays close to home. Even told to look elsewhere, it picks Computer Science for most ideas.
numbers: Free-Form baseline: 947 occurrences of Computer Science, normalized domain entropy 0.326. Guided Dual-Retrieval 0.812; Idea-Catalyst 0.682 (more diverse than free-form, less than dual, but with better novelty).
limits: More domain spread did not mean more insight; picking sources well mattered more.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence of near-field bias in model retrieval. Needs a coded constraint on source distance.

source: Kargupta, Mehri, Hakkani-Tur, Han (2026) Idea-Catalyst
finding: Human check with six PhD researchers on their own problems found the tool useful for finding research questions; reported verbosity.
numbers: N=6. Relevance of generated research questions 4.00/5; retrieved papers 3.50/5.
limits: Six people, self-chosen problems, no control arm.
agent_relevance: Weak human validation; treat the LLM-judge gains as unconfirmed.

source: Chen, Wang, Wang (2026) ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
finding: 200-task benchmark of far analogies from real-world concepts to grid transformations. Models trail humans; analogical prompting plus vision helped some models, not all.
numbers: Humans average 68.96% (+typo) / 58.35% (strict); top-2-attempt human 93.5-96%. Models (pass@3): GPT 5.2 best at roughly 48-51%; Claude Opus 4.5 about 7-9%. Gaps vs humans reliable by paired bootstrap, CIs exclude zero. Pulley category: Gemini 100% analogy correctness, GPT 0%.
limits: Results table garbled in the text layer, so exact cell mapping is uncertain. Models run at their default reasoning effort.
agent_relevance: Far analogy remains hard for frontier models; do not assume retrieval plus mapping works across distant domains.

source: Chen, Wang, Wang (2026) ARCANA, ConceptSIR
finding: ConceptSIR loop (concept proposal, slippage, execution, introspection, refinement with code-run prediction error) solved half of a hard subset. Uses Gemini 3 Pro for concepts and GPT 5.2 for code.
numbers: 9 of 17 hard tasks solved in 7 of 11 categories; 5-loop budget; 2.22 loops on average for solved cases; one run per task.
limits: 17 tasks picked with preference for low direct-LLM accuracy; authors say it is not general because it needs code execution.
agent_relevance: Supports the schema pattern: analogy proposal followed by running the mapping and mutating on observed error.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang (2024) AutoTRIZ
finding: LLM pipeline runs TRIZ steps (contradiction, inventive principles, solution) and produces a report. Checked against textbook expert analyses; an entropy score tracks diversity of the model's contradiction choices.
numbers: 7 of 10 textbook cases matched or half-matched in the top 3 detected contradictions; higher-probability outputs matched better. Battery thermal case: designed heat-pipe system +24% to +64% on metrics vs best existing scheme (computed by the authors).
limits: Ten cases; textbook answer is not ground truth. Design evaluation was by the authors' own models.
agent_relevance: TRIZ is a rule-based abstraction route to cross-domain principles; majority voting over contradictions is a usable consistency check.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT
finding: Four prompt styles tested for TRIZ contradiction analysis with GPT-4: basic, CoT, few-shot, CoT plus few-shot. Few-shot lowered recall.
numbers: 34 cases (3 used for few-shot). Recall: basic 0.675, CoT 0.691, few-shot 0.245, CoT+few-shot 0.247. Precision 0.259, 0.310, 0.333, 0.298. For at least half of contradiction parameters: 85.3% of cases (basic), 88.2% (CoT).
limits: Ground truth is the contradiction pairs the cited papers happened to list, so precision is understated by design.
agent_relevance: Examples can narrow the search (model copies the count of items in the examples). Another case where less scaffold gave wider retrieval.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT
finding: For solution generation from a chosen inventive principle, prompt style made no difference; GPT-4 reached high similarity to the published solutions with all four.
numbers: 84 cases. Cosine similarity (ada-002) base M=0.829 SD 0.031; CoT 0.823; few-shot 0.824; CoT+few-shot 0.824. GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 tested on 10 post-April-2023 cases.
limits: Embedding similarity to a known solution rewards recall of known answers, not invention.
agent_relevance: Do not expect prompt tricks to change mapping quality once the principle is given.

source: Kulikowski (2026) Same Problem, Different Field
finding: Re-describing each paper as a domain-stripped mechanism skeleton (one cached LLM call) lets cross-field retrieval find papers solving the same computation. Trained scientific embedders did worse than plain TF-IDF on abstracts.
numbers: Benchmark: 18 method families, 109 papers. Average precision on abstract 0.222 to skeleton 0.513; whole fingerprint 0.557 (95% CI 0.407-0.720). SPECTER lowest at 0.095, lifted to 0.334 by the fingerprint. Wild corpus of 501 papers: blind LLM judges rate 8 of top 30 pairs genuine vs 0 of 30 random.
limits: Small benchmark, judges are LLMs, four executed imports as human check. Distilled by a small hosted model.
agent_relevance: Strongest recent evidence for abstraction-before-retrieval. Retrieve on function, not on topic words.

source: Jung et al. (2026) Cross-Pollination Retrieval
finding: Benchmark of 1,300 queries across 26 fields for finding transferable ideas. Off-the-shelf retrievers fail; an LLM reranker does far better; fine-tuning on cross-field citation pairs closes most of the gap.
numbers: Best of 11 retrievers Recall@10 0.26 (chance 0.07); LLM reranker 0.81; fine-tuned Qwen3-Embedding-4B 0.70, 0.6B from 0.12 to 0.50. AnaloBench nDCG@10 up to +33% over untrained; training on three standard retrieval sets lowered it. BRIGHT up to +70%. HyDE with BM25 raised Recall@10 from 0.16 to 0.44.
limits: Relevance defined by citation links, which are a proxy for transferable ideas.
agent_relevance: A reranker call is the right place to spend model compute in analogue search; plain embeddings retrieve topic, not transfer.

source: Ye et al. (2024) AnaloBench (EMNLP)
finding: Pick the analogous story among four (T1), at 1, 10 and 30 sentences. Models drop sharply with length; humans stay near flat; no model beat humans anywhere.
numbers: T1 accuracy 1/10/30 sentences: GPT-4 89.1/66.5/60.7; GPT-3.5 65.3/46.4/30.8; Claude 68.2/30.2/25.9; Tulu2-70B 71.8/51.2/31.5; Human 96.0/72.5/73.3; random 25. Human-GPT-4 gap 6.9 points at 1 sentence, 28.8 at 30 (as the paper states).
limits: 30-sentence human numbers from 30 items. Stories extended by GPT-4, but GPT-4 stayed similar on Claude-written stories (60.7 vs 57.6).
agent_relevance: Real analogues are long and messy; short toy analogies overstate model skill.

source: Ye et al. (2024) AnaloBench
finding: Retrieving analogues from a large bank (T2) was close to random for long stories. Bigger models stopped helping on long stories.
numbers: Retrieval of top-10 analogues from a bank of 200+ stories: GPT-4 and Claude near the trivial random baseline except GPT-4-Turbo at 1 sentence; MAP values in the low single digits. Model-size gains plateau for 10- and 30-sentence T1.
limits: No human T2 run (too much reading). Only two long-context models fit the bank.
agent_relevance: Do not ask the model to pick the best analogue from a long list; pre-filter with code and compare in short pairs.

source: Li et al. (2025) Past Meets Present: Creating Historical Analogy with LLMs
finding: Free generation of historical analogues beat retrieval from a finite dataset; a self-reflection loop that checks candidates for hallucination and stereotype gave the best scores. Stereotype means picking events with the same actors rather than the same idea.
numbers: Free generation beat retrieval by an average of 0.25 (their metric). Llama3.1-8B and GPT-3.5, temperature 0.1. Reflection ran in only about 10% of cases; more than five candidates added tokens but little gain; extra warm-up rounds can reduce results.
limits: Metrics are LLM-judged multi-dimension scores; human eval ranked reflection first. Table cells garbled.
agent_relevance: Candidate set plus selection plus a check, with reflection that is rarely triggered, fits our doubt-only-on-signal rule.

source: Luu and Buehler (2023) BioinspiredLLM
finding: Llama-2-13B fine-tuned on over 1,000 biological and bio-inspired materials papers (about 98% article yield). Better recall of biology than the base chat model; retrieval from the paper set added further, especially for numeric facts.
numbers: 100 multiple-choice questions (general, specific, non-biological, numerical). BioinspiredLLM baseline 82%, about 90% with a think-step-by-step prefix. RAG version scored top across categories.
limits: Exam written by the authors; only one 100-item test; no hypothesis was tested in the lab.
agent_relevance: A domain-tuned or retrieval-grounded biology store is more reliable than a general model recalling biology unaided.

source: Buehler (2023) Diatom-inspired architected materials using language-based deep learning
finding: Transformer-based language model used to generate diatom-like structures, with one design manufactured by additive manufacturing.
numbers: One design built; no retrieval-quality metric.
limits: Generation, not retrieval; proof of concept.
agent_relevance: Shows physical follow-through exists for LLM-aided bio-inspired work, but not an analogue-retrieval result.
